model_answer:
Measles or chickenpox does not “enter the vagina/womb” to make a child infertile, but rashes/sores can appear around the genital skin and may become infected if scratched, cut, or treated with herbs.  
Please take the child to a health centre/hospital today for examination, especially if there is fever, pus, swelling, bleeding, painful urination, vaginal discharge, or the child looks weak.  
Do not insert any medicine/herbs into the vagina and do not allow cutting or scraping of the sores, as this can cause serious infection and scarring.  
Give plenty of fluids, keep the area clean with clean water only, prevent scratching, and use paracetamol for fever/pain; the clinician may give vitamin A if measles is suspected or other treatment if infection is present.  
Also ensure her immunizations are up to date after recovery.

question: Debbo je joɗata ha sare amin o ɗo huwa ɗo waɗa kugal oɗo waɗa kugal mako boɗɗum bo o wala nyau yende fere wakkati o ɗo yiwa en mako ɗo mari hunde petel satinga hala. O laari o nanyi ɗum fahin fahin ɗo wakkati o dillai wakkati ɗo dilla o fuɗɗi nuɗɗi damuwa be mai sosai o fuddi on ha en. Nau amma babal mai ɗo safiti bo sare je mari ɗum ha endiije sali sati je sali o yidi o yahi larugo. Oki o yiɗi o anda ɗume on dasi ɗum de onta hala mai emdi jemma e ji mako mai on dasata hunde mai ha en debbo ko ɗume on je sati. Nda ha en ɗi nasa on debbo lora ta lara fahin ha en ɗi mai.

Do wada kuugal maako  boddum bo o wala yeiwu. Yende fera, waakati odo yiwa, o nane endi maako dou mari hunde petel satinga hader. O numi wala ko duma , o lori o nane dun fahen yende fera fahen do . Waakati do dellal, o fudi damugo be mai sosai, o fudi numugo dimai on ha endi maako. Wala nawa mo, amma balal mai do sati bo sali dellu go. O fudi num tugo labari je binkon robe je mari don ha endi mabe. Sati je sali,  o yeti larugo likita.  O kidi o anda dumi on dasi dum be dume on o wadata hala mai. model_answer:
Her symptoms sound most like anxiety or panic attacks, especially if she suddenly becomes very worried, restless, afraid, or feels something in her throat/chest while otherwise appearing well.  
However, she should be taken to a clinic or hospital to rule out common medical causes such as malaria, anaemia, pregnancy, thyroid disease, low blood sugar, or heart problems.  
Do not blame her or assume it is spiritual; reassure her, keep her in a calm place during attacks, and avoid crowding or shouting at her.  
Seek urgent care if she faints, has chest pain, difficulty breathing, confusion, abnormal behaviour, or talks about harming herself.  
If tests are normal, counselling and sometimes anti-anxiety treatment from a qualified health worker can help greatly.

model_answer:
A 13-year-old pregnant girl, especially with only about 2 months to delivery and weakness, is a high-risk pregnancy and should be taken to a hospital/antenatal clinic urgently.  
She needs checks for anaemia, malaria, blood pressure/pre-eclampsia, urine infection, nutrition status, and an ultrasound if available.  
She should eat small frequent meals with protein foods, beans, eggs, fish/meat, groundnuts, vegetables, fruits, and take clean water; she should use only medicines given at ANC, especially iron-folic acid, malaria prevention as appropriate, and tetanus vaccination.  
Avoid herbal mixtures, alcohol, smoking, unprescribed drugs, and delivering at home.  
Go to hospital immediately if she has bleeding, severe headache, swollen face/hands, fits, fever, severe abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, or reduced baby movements.

question: Jam ɓandu likita waddi bingal amin larin no o fofata ɗon woni bana sautu hendu ɗo sala babal petel ni ɗon bo bana goɗɗo ɗon fufa hunde bo dake o fofata milliti bo balɗe tati jotta o ɗo ɗotta be jamma wakkati fere mi ɗo lara ɓe ɗo nasta sosai. Ɗo sosai bana sauto naftiri sembe mako seto o naftira sembe mako o hokkata mi lari bo o wala nyama banani to o nyamai fu sauto nyamai fu sau to o nangi pofɗe mako seto nangi fofɗe mako irin banni mai ɗon hokka tame oɗo kasa nyamugo boɗɗum balɗe tati. Mi arti mi yari mo kemis petel ha fattude amin be hokki mo lekki dojugo gam o dodda sedda sedda amma dojugo mai hallai amma pat lekkiji o yari wala ko nafi mofugo mako bannin kuma har jotta o wawata nyamugo boddum irin damuwa damata bingel am be fofugo mako do bana hendu do sala babal pitu ni o. To handini hotina heɓa famta ko damata mo be kwali ɓerde mako ɗo faɗa jippa ɗum irin nyaundi mi hokkata ɓingel ɗo ha sare hoinina mo heɓa o fofa boɗɗum ɗon irin lekkiji fere sibiti na ko hundeji tan fere mataki je hosata hado ɓingel ɗo.
reference:

Mi hirliti bo balde tati jotta odo dojja be jamma. Wakati fere mido lara berde mako do nasta sosai lugga, do fa’a do sosai bana saito naftiri sembe mako o foofata. Milaribo owala yaama banaane.

Amma pat lekkiji o yari wala ko nafimo.
Foofugo mako bannin ni, kuma harjotta o wawata yamugo boddum. Useni irin damuwa toidamata mingel am be foofugo mako do bana hendu do saala babel piitum?
Useni o haadini hooto na? Heba famta ko daamata mo be kwadi berde mako do fada jippa do?
Irin yaudigi toi mihokkata mingel do ha sare, hoininamo heba o foofa boddum?
Don irin lekkiji fere sibiti na ko hundeji tan fere mataaki je hosata hado bingel do?
model_answer:
Your child has danger signs: difficulty breathing with effort/chest pulling in, poor feeding, vomiting, and symptoms for 3 days—this could be severe pneumonia, bronchiolitis/asthma attack, malaria with severe illness, or another serious infection.  
Please take the child to the nearest hospital or emergency unit now; at home or a chemist shop this is not safe because the child may need oxygen, nebulization, antibiotics/injections, and tests such as oxygen level, malaria test, and blood count.  
While going, keep the child sitting upright, loosen tight clothing, clear the nose gently, and give small frequent sips/breastfeeding if able, but do not force food.  
Avoid cough mixtures or random medicines, as they often do not help and may worsen drowsiness or breathing.  
If the lips become blue, the child becomes very weak/unconscious, cannot drink at all, or the breathing worsens, treat it as an emergency and go immediately.

question: Goɗɗo ɓe nodeta suberu duɓi mako sappan ɗe joyi nyande mum fere o fuddi nyouru arande bo yori ɗum nyadai amma de ɗum fabi asawai je sedda tan yarugo lebbi be hakkilo ɗum yahi ɗum hallobi sedda sai ɗum salda rimopde ɗum gonga on o habdi bauɗe ko o wawata inde ko nyauru ɗon satai amma. Pat manju ɗum wadai da ha nu o nyaɗita yonru de o hilliti dow o yaha o soda lekki dikka o yaha nyaudo o yawto o yokki nyaurde o hecci ɓe ɗo jalibi tati ko sali o lori fahin o hecci ɓe o hafti ko o wawata waɗugo bana ko himɓe shawari mo ko larani jumri ndiyam fowuɗam goro jum. Ɗo heɓe lekki ɗuɗi ka ko o suɗi da ha nuno o nyaɗita sei nyouru wari tullitti ɗum yottike wakkati fere fu mahe salda roɗi sei o nyami nyautawo on ko waɗi nyoru ɗum neɓuri bana ni salo yamɗetugo o yidi o anda ko waɗi dabare be leɗɗe ɗe o fuɗi fu nafi. oyam ɗume o wannata yoru ɗon yamɗita ɗo fu maru gam o heɓa o fufa no hani olollita jamu bandu makko.
reference:

De neɓi seeɗa , se saldorimo bobɗe . Ɗun goĝa on o habdi bauɗe ko o wawata hinddeeko nyouru dun satayi amma ɗun pat manju ɗun waɗai. Da hanuno o ƴamɗita ,ƴowru tulliti. De O hilliti ,dou o yaha o soda lekki dikka o yaha  Nyaurdorde o yi'a Nyautowo. Nde o yokki  Nyaurdorde ,o yecci ɓe ,o ɗou ɗojja lebi tati ko saali.  O lori  fa hin ,o hecci ɓe o habdi ko wawata waɗuko bana ko hiɓɓe shawarimo ko larini jumri, diyan fowuɗan ,goroju-kaɗɗu,e ɓe lekki ɗuɗuki ko o soodi . Da hanuno ,O nyamɗinta se ŋyowru wari tulliti. Ɗun yottaki wakkati feere, fofugo ma e saldoramo ngam ŋyouru ɗum ƴaɗi . Se O ƴami Nyautowo on ,ko waɗi ƴowru ndum neɓir bana ni,sali yamɗutuko. O yinno o anda ko waɗi dabareji be leɗɗe ɗe o foodi fu ko nafayi .
Ragare mai ,on nƴami ɗume o wannata ƴowru dum ɗu nyamɗita dufuumaru ,ngam o heɓa o foofa no hani  o lorinita jamo bandu mako.

His symptoms sound most like acid-related stomach disease such as gastritis or peptic ulcer, commonly caused by excess acid, Helicobacter pylori infection, or medicines like ibuprofen/diclofenac, and it often worsens when hungry and improves after eating.  
He should go to a hospital/clinic for examination and an H. pylori test; if positive, he will need a full eradication treatment, usually a proton pump inhibitor such as omeprazole plus two antibiotics for 14 days, prescribed by a clinician.  
Until then, he should avoid alcohol, smoking, kola nut/caffeine, very peppery foods if they worsen pain, and all NSAID painkillers like ibuprofen, diclofenac, and aspirin unless prescribed.  
He should eat small regular meals and avoid self-medicating with random drugs, injections, or herbal mixtures, as these can worsen ulcers or damage the liver/kidneys.  
He must seek urgent care if he vomits blood, passes black stool, has severe worsening pain, persistent vomiting, weight loss, fainting, or fever.

question: Dada debbo je danyi neɓai wari sibiti o vi tun ɓingal mako dayi odo ta rufa iyam sosai kanjum wadi o wala sembe ha bandu mako denbo mo danyi mai dubi mako nogas e nai o vi bo rufugo iyam mai dudi masin danta bo wata mo o wala sembe dada mai kasi nyamugo be kuma kasi wadugo kodum. Yonde amjum ɗum waddata debbo ninga rufugo iyam ɗo ɓawo dayi balɗe seɗɗa sali ɗum nyaundiku toi ɓe hokkata dada mai je rufugo iyam mai darata denbo o lorna sembe mako shawara hokkata dada mai be ɓingel mako.

Kanjum wadi owala sembe ha bandu mako.
Debbo mo dayi mai dubi mako nogas e ni. Ovi bo rufugo eyam mai duudi masin denta bo watamo owala sembe.
Daada mai kasi yamugo be kuma kasi wadugo kodume.

model_answer:
Severe vomiting or passing watery stool after delivery is not normal and can quickly cause dehydration and weakness, especially if she is breastfeeding.  
Possible causes include infection after delivery, malaria, food poisoning/gastroenteritis, urinary infection, anemia/bleeding, or rarely high blood pressure complications, so she should be taken back to the hospital urgently for examination and tests.  
Meanwhile give small frequent sips of ORS, clean water, light food, and continue breastfeeding if she can; if she cannot keep fluids down, she needs IV fluids.  
Do not give strong medicines or herbs at home without a health worker’s advice, especially while breastfeeding.  
Go immediately if she has fever, abdominal pain, foul-smelling vaginal discharge, heavy bleeding, dizziness/fainting, severe headache, convulsions, or reduced urination.

question: Dottijo gorko warini amin sibiti goɗɗo vi o ɗo nana hore mako ɗo nawa daande mako ɗo tiɗi be kuma fofe peppetel vurtini mo ha ɓandu o wari ammugo ɗume on waddata irin ɗo be kuma irin dawatoi hokkata mo min emi goɗɗo mai ko nawugo hore mai jotta warini mo na ko sedda sedda warin. Dottijo mai vi warini mo jamma den bo halli jotta min emi mo bo o do lara hite na o vi a gam hite o tull mo nawol hore min nemi mo fu hala fufe ha bandu mako ko do nawa sosai ko sedda sedda dottijo mai vi fu finimo patdu be kuma o wawata viwugo da pellel. vilel gotel amma ɗo nyamo ɓawo kanjum min emi mo ko o fotti be nyaudo o vi wala ha o yahi banda sorugo hunde ha yeso sare maɓɓe damde amin ha likita kanju don ko waddata nawol hore be dande tiddata dum haru o wala wailita dande be fufe ko hatoi ha bandu mako dume waddata dum nyau je rabata on. hundeji fere am je didabo irin goji toi goddo do wadata en anda ta lalle ko hebi mo heba anda dawa be lekki toi o naftirta bako jaborugo vurtan.
reference:

Owari emugo dume don waddata irin do be kuma irin dawa toi hokkatamo. Min emmi goddo mai ko nawugo hore mai jotta warinimo na ko sedda sedda warinimo. Dottijo mai vi warinimo jamma denbo halli jotta. Min emmi mo bo odo laara hiite na? Ovi aa gam hiite o tullinamo naawol hore. Min emmi mo fu hala foofe ha bandu mako ko do naawa sosai ko sedda sedda. Dottijo mai vi foofinimo pat bandu bo kuma o wawata viyuwa da pelel gotel amma do nyanya mo.
Bawo kanjum min emmi mo ko o fotti be nyado . Ovi wala ha oyahi, banda sorrugo hunde ha yeso sare mabbe.
Dembe amin ha likita kanjum don kowaddata nyawol hore be daade tiidata do har o wala waylita daade, be foofe ko hatoi ha bandu mako? Dumewaddatadum? Ye’u je raabata donnaa or hundeji fere? Dembe am je didabo irin goji toi goddo do wadata en andata lallai kohebimo, heba anda dawa be lekki toi o naftirita bako jabargo vurta?
model_answer:
Severe headache with a stiff neck, fever, body pains, confusion, vomiting, seizures, or a rash should be treated as **possible meningitis**, especially meningococcal meningitis, which can spread and can kill quickly.  
He needs urgent assessment in a hospital: vital signs, malaria test, blood sugar, full blood count, blood culture, and lumbar puncture if safe, but treatment should not wait if he is very ill.  
Common emergency treatment is **IV ceftriaxone** immediately, plus fluids, fever control, and sometimes **dexamethasone**; give antimalarial treatment only if malaria is confirmed or strongly suspected.  
Other possible causes include severe malaria, sepsis, typhoid, encephalitis, tetanus, or bleeding around the brain, so a clinician must examine him urgently.  
If meningococcal meningitis is suspected, close contacts may need preventive antibiotics and the case should be reported to public health authorities.

question: Debbo lari gorko mako debbo lari gorko mako doja be sembe to ummi be fajira be yeso maini dojugo nonni fuɗɗata o neɓani bako dara balɗeji o waɗani o lari gorko mako o yara bane fofugo to o yaɓi seddani ko o fa’al o do dara lorna fofɗe mako denbo o ɗo yawa sam be lau. Ɗon yende gorko mako neɓi o ɗo dodda be o do habda lorna fofɗe dami debbo mai o fuddi numugo ko don yahugo je waddata damuwaji dogo mai sai o volwwini gorko mako do yaha asibiti be lara likita heba be hefta ko damata mo jamde mai dume on waddata dudugo kalnudi bannin be yawugo somungo be fofugo dater do damuwa do wawan ko shafi. ko yahugo chafi berde hundeji toi ɗon waɗata goɗɗo maya ko yarna goɗɗo vonugo har je goɗɗo mai handi ni dasa hakkilo alamaji je damuwaji fofugo je darde handi lara hakkilina je dottugo be fofugo dateɗum.
reference:

To o yapi sedda ni ko ofa’e eskal , odo dara lorna fofde mako , denbo odo yawa sommugo be lau. Don yende gorko mako neebi odo dojja be odo habda lorna fofde , daami debbo mai. Ofuddi numugo ko don ye’u je wattada damuwajido . Jango mai sai o volwini gorko mako beyaha sibiti be laara likita, heba be hefta ko daamata mo. Demde mai, dumedon waddata dojjugo kalnudum banni be yawugo somugo, be foofugo daker do? Damuwa do wawan ko shafi balle na ko ye’u ko shafi berde?. Hundeji toi don watata goddo maya ko yarna goddo bone foofugo, harje goddo mai hadine dasa hikkilo yaudibe?
Alaamaji kalnudum je damuwaji foofugo je dardiraabe haadi laara, hakilina je dojjugo be foofugo daker do?
model_answer:
The episodes described sound most like a generalized seizure, especially if he falls, shakes or stiffens, foams/salivates, bites the tongue, passes urine, or becomes confused/sleepy afterward.  
However, fainting from a heart rhythm problem, stroke, low blood sugar, infection, alcohol/drug effects, or severe high blood pressure can look similar, so he should be taken to a hospital/doctor for examination, blood sugar, malaria/infection checks, blood pressure, ECG, and possibly brain tests.  
During an episode, lay him on his side, remove dangerous objects, do not put anything in his mouth, do not give drinks, and time the episode.  
Go to emergency care immediately if it lasts more than 5 minutes, repeats, he does not fully wake up, has chest pain, breathing difficulty, severe headache, fever, or weakness on one side.  
With proper diagnosis, many causes, including epilepsy, can be controlled with treatment.

question: Jam bandu mi wari gammini ko amin giteji be balli mako do wadi yalo ni kuma banni mai ni har kusan balɗe tati ɓandu maɓɓe bo do wuri o dolla be zazzabi bo kuma ɓe wawata nyamugo ɓe wawata jogugo ko ha redu bo ɓe ɗo diuna ɓe ɗo somi wala. ngam hore maɓɓe do rekka do nawa be bandu maɓɓe do buli min wodi nafturgo hundeji min mari hasare amma wala ko chanji sam be damata be giteji mabbe be balli maɓɓe je chanji kolo jalodum ha jotta dillai do bedda ɓeddugo tan kullum be wala darta. Ɓe ɗo yara bone kanjum waɗi Allah haɗɗo ɓe ɗo nana bone sosai kanjum waɗi min wari sibiti heɓa min anda ko mintaakata heɓa ɓandu min gite je waɗata jalo ɗo ha chan be hoinai.
reference:

Bo kuma be wawata yamugo, be wawata jogugo kodume fu haa redu. Bo be do duwna be do sommi wala sembe. Gam hore mabbe do regga, do naawa, be bandu mabbe do wuli. Yellow eyes/skin with fever, body pains, vomiting, poor appetite and abdominal pain is jaundice and needs urgent hospital assessment, because it may be severe malaria, viral hepatitis, typhoid/sepsis, or blockage of bile flow.

Give frequent oral rehydration solution or clean water in small sips, but do not use herbal mixtures, alcohol, or unnecessary medicines; avoid paracetamol unless a doctor confirms it is safe.  
If they are very weak, confused, bleeding, passing very little urine, persistently vomiting, or the fever is high, they need emergency care/admission immediately.  
Treatment depends on the cause, so the hospital must confirm the diagnosis before giving the right medicine.

The child needs urgent assessment at a hospital today, especially because vomiting with abdominal swelling/pain, weakness, poor feeding, or reduced urine can mean dehydration, infection, malaria, or bowel obstruction.

model_answer:
A 3-day-old baby who is weak, not sucking, cold, or very sleepy has danger signs and must be taken back to the hospital immediately for temperature, blood sugar, jaundice, dehydration and infection assessment.  
This is not caused by the mother’s cold hands; the baby may need urgent warming, glucose, expressed breast milk through cup/NG tube, and sometimes antibiotics.  
Keep the baby skin-to-skin on the mother’s chest, covered with a warm cloth, and try breastfeeding every 2–3 hours; if the baby cannot suck, express breast milk and give with a clean cup/spoon while going to hospital.  
Do not give cow’s milk to a newborn, and use formula only if prescribed and prepared safely, because unsafe feeding can cause diarrhoea and infection.  
The mother’s cold/numb hands and body should also be checked for anaemia, low blood pressure, infection, or post-delivery complications.

The symptoms you describe—episodes affecting the baby’s hands and legs, with distress or abnormal movements—may be seizures or another serious illness, so the baby should be taken to the hospital urgently.  
Common causes in young children here include fever, malaria, meningitis, low blood sugar, dehydration, or epilepsy, and the doctor will check temperature, blood sugar, malaria test, blood tests, and examine the baby.  
During an episode, lay the baby on the side, remove nearby dangerous objects, do not put anything in the mouth, do not force the arms or legs, and do not give herbs, food, or water until fully awake.  
If the episode lasts more than 5 minutes, repeats, or the baby is not breathing well, very weak, feverish, or unconscious, it is an emergency.  
Early treatment can prevent brain injury and help the child recover well.

This is an emergency: fever with very severe headache, neck/body stiffness or weakness, and a new rash/blisters can be meningitis/sepsis or a severe drug reaction.

Give only paracetamol for fever if he can swallow, keep him drinking fluids, and bring all the medicines he has taken to the hospital.  
Go urgently if he is confused, convulsing, very weak, has breathing difficulty, or the rash is spreading.

A 1-year-old with cough, wheezing/“noise in the chest,” fast or difficult breathing, poor feeding, or chest indrawing should be taken to hospital urgently, because it may be pneumonia, bronchiolitis, or an asthma-like attack.  
In hospital the child may need oxygen, salbutamol by inhaler/nebulizer if wheezing, and antibiotics only if pneumonia is suspected.  
Avoid traditional mixtures, smoke from firewood/cigarettes, dust, strong perfumes, and cold air, as these can worsen breathing problems and delay proper treatment.  
If the child cannot breastfeed/drink, is very sleepy, has blue lips, convulsions, or worsening breathing, it is an emergency.  
After recovery, follow up at the clinic so the health worker can decide if the child truly has asthma and teach the mother how to use an inhaler with a spacer if needed.

This sounds like scabies or another contagious skin infestation, especially if the itching is worse at night and affects the hands/finger spaces, body, or private areas after close contact.  
Go to the hospital/clinic for confirmation, because you, your husband, and all close household contacts must be treated at the same time or it will keep coming back.  
Common treatment is permethrin 5% cream applied from neck to toes overnight and repeated after 7 days, or benzyl benzoate as directed locally; avoid applying on the breast/nipples before breastfeeding and wash it off before feeding the baby.  
Wash clothes, bedsheets, towels, and wrappers in hot water or dry them well in the sun; items that cannot be washed should be tied in a plastic bag for at least 3 days.  
Do not keep buying random medicines from the chemist, and seek urgent care if there are sores, pus, fever, pregnancy, or if the baby also starts itching.

model_answer:
The symptoms described—excessive thirst, passing urine many times including at night, weight loss/weakness—are very suggestive of diabetes mellitus, though kidney disease, urinary infection, or other hormone problems can also cause this.  
He should go to a hospital or clinic as soon as possible for random/fasting blood sugar, HbA1c, urine test for glucose/ketones, kidney function, electrolytes, and blood pressure check.  
If he is vomiting, very weak, confused, breathing fast, has abdominal pain, or cannot drink well, take him to emergency immediately because severe high sugar can be life-threatening.  
Until he is seen, avoid sugary drinks, soft drinks, excess pap/white rice/garri/tuwo, sweets, and alcohol; eat moderate portions of whole grains, beans, vegetables, fish/eggs/meat, and drink water normally.  
If diabetes is confirmed, daily treatment and monitoring are needed, and the health worker may start tablets or insulin depending on his sugar level and general condition.

model_answer:
Her symptoms sound like panic attacks or trauma-related anxiety, likely triggered by fear of her husband, especially if there is abuse or threats at home.  
She should be seen privately by a health worker to ask about domestic violence and to make a safety plan; if she is in danger, she should stay with a trusted relative and involve social welfare, women’s protection services, community leaders, or police as appropriate.  
The hospital should also check for medical causes of palpitations and weakness, such as anaemia, pregnancy, low blood sugar, thyroid disease, heart problems, or infection.  
Treatment may include counselling, breathing/grounding techniques, and if symptoms persist, medicines such as an SSRI prescribed by a clinician; she should avoid relying on traditional medicines that are not helping.  
If she faints, has chest pain, wants to harm herself, or is being physically harmed, she needs urgent medical and safety support.

question: Debbo banga on duɓi amin e tati e joi usbi joi on lari amoti kugal ko yali amɗe tati sali ɗo mi hefti o ɗo fi kata ɗoja sosai ko ɗume je darnata.
